messages:
marco: Heads up — since ~09:10 UTC we're seeing a big uptick in remote_write errors from ap-southeast-1: repeated `502`/`connection reset` and the remote_write queue length jumped on a few pushgateway/sidecar nodes. graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc/remote-write-queue?orgId=1 :alarm:
amber: saw the same. NAT gw logs show a burst of ephemeral port exhaustion + lots of TIME_WAIT. Could be fanout from autoscaled GPU pods hitting the same natgw.
jonathan: confirmed on the kube-proxy nodes too — conntrack table shows many CLOSE_WAIT entries for our exporter endpoints. p95 latency for remote_write shot from 120ms -> 1.4s.
li: copying the prom config for the failing cluster: ```remote_write:
  - url: "https://cortex.ap-southeast-1.redwood/api/prom/push"
    remote_timeout: 30s
    queue_config:
      max_samples_per_send: 1000
      max_shards: 200
      capacity: 50000
```  we haven't touched max_shards/capacity in months.
kevin: can you paste a snippet of relabeling rules? I'm worried about high-cardinality exporter labels (pod annotations + gpu_serial) suddenly exploding.
marco: the exporter images autoscaled because of a job burst. relabels are minimal right now: we only drop `__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_*` for some services, nothing for annotations or `gpu_serial`.
amber: quick mitigation idea: add relabel_config to drop pod annotations and drop `gpu_serial` label at scrape time. e.g.
```yaml
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_annotation_prometheus_io_scrape]
    regex: "(false)"
    action: drop
  - source_labels: [gpu_serial]
    regex: ".+"
    action: labelmap
  - target_label: gpu_serial
    regex: ".+"
    action: drop
```
li: small correction — using `labelmap` then `drop` is redundant; you can drop directly with `action: drop` using `source_labels`->`regex: .+`. also be careful with labelmap, might expand into more labels.
jonathan: Ops-side immediate steps I recommend:
- add a short-term relabel to drop gpu_serial and export annotations
- reduce `max_samples_per_send` to 500 and `capacity` to 20000 to reduce per-request payloads
- bump `remote_timeout` to 60s only if backend handles it (we should avoid lengthening if NAT gw is choking)
- scale natgw/egress nodes per AZ and enable port mapping splay

marco: implementing a drop relabel now to staging and will roll to canary. pushing a small prom config change: ```- action: drop
  source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_gpu_serial]
  regex: ".+"```
ops-bot: deploy started: prom-configs/remotewrite-droplabels -> staging at 09:26 UTC :rocket:
amber: Also propose tuning alerts — r/w queue length flapping caused pager storms. We should make an alert that requires sustained 5m+ queue growth and correlate with natgw port free ratio and conntrack entries.
kevin: agree. Also add a Grafana panel for ephemeral port usage by natgw + conntrack state counts per node. helps distinguish app-level flood vs infra issue.
li: longer term: consider sharding remote_write per-region or per-tenant, and add per-exporter prefix/KV caching for common prefixes; and implement a relabeling policy in our onboarding template to drop any unique hardware ids by default.
jonathan: rolled to canary — saw immediate drop in queue length on canary cluster and 502s reduced. still watching ap-southeast-1 for other hotspots.
marco: thanks, baseline is back to normal on canary. planning full rollout in 15min after smoke checks. will follow up with postmortem if anything else shows up.
amber: nice work. please file a short postmortem + action items: natgw capacity runbook, add default relabels to exporter helm chart, and alert tuning.
marco: will file. tagging @kevin for runbook and @li for default helm relabel PR.
ops-bot: deploy succeeded: prom-configs/remotewrite-droplabels -> canary at 09:39 UTC :white_check_mark:
kevin: starting a quick runbook draft now. thanks everyone.
